pr_title: Add option to suppress log in exception handler

issue_context.title: ExceptionHandlerMiddleware should allow more customizabiltiy of logging
issue_context.body:
I want to use `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware` (via `UseExceptionHandler`) for my exception handling.  Whilst it allows me to run custom code when generating the HTTP response, there appears to be no customizability when it comes to logging:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/5e575a3e64254932c1fd4937041a4e7426afcde4/src/Middleware/Diagnostics/src/ExceptionHandler/ExceptionHandlerMiddleware.cs#L92

The middleware always logs "An unhandled exception has occurred while executing the request." with the exception.  I think there should at least be an option I can pass in to prevent this middleware logging anything, so I can output my own logging (I wish to log the `Path` too, obtained from `IExceptionHandlerPathFeature`), and maybe an option to get `ExceptionHandlerMiddleware` to log the `Path` itself.
comments: Seems reasonable as an option to disable logging.
Isn't this already possible via config?

@davidfowl A couple of things: while that'll work with .NET Core's default logging architecture, "None" might not be an option for all logging frameworks.  I don't think Serilog has that option, for example.  Also, it just looks rather unintuative semantically, because it kind of looks like you're trying to configure your app NOT to log unhandled exceptions.

> @davidfowl A couple of things: while that'll work with .NET Core's default logging architecture, "None" might not be an option for all logging frameworks.

2 things:
- Logging filtering is handled by the factory by default, so if you use *any* logging provider it will work. 
- Serilog happens to implement an entire ILoggerFactory and there's a serilog specific way to disable categories.

> Also, it just looks rather unintuative semantically, because it kind of looks like you're trying to configure your app NOT to log unhandled exceptions.

I agree it's not as intuitive as an option on the middleware itself but I disagree it not telling your app the log exceptions. The logging category is clearly scoped to the middleware which makes it specific.

The fact that there is a way to do this today makes this a low priority but if you want to send a pull request with a new set of options that apply to this middleware I would happily review it.

I've just been reading: https://github.com/serilog/serilog-extensions-logging/issues/98

Interestinly you yourself seem to be saying that `UseSerilog` is breaking things in ASP.NET Core, @davidfowl .  It overrides ASP.NET's filtering and throws everything over to Serilog, which provides an inferior filtering experience:
https://github.com/serilog/serilog-extensions-logging/blob/c5bad0c183ae10d448fcc3532095e298d57906a1/src/Serilog.Extensions.Logging/SerilogLoggingBuilderExtensions.cs#L49

Seems like they've made some rather crap decisions about integrating with .NET Core.  I'm gonna have to review whether I wanna use Serilog.
Anyhow, it'd still be good if the exception handling middleware could take a config that made it not log anything.

Just in case anyone else is following along and wondering how Serilog handles filtering, see https://github.com/serilog/serilog-filters-expressions#serilogfiltersexpressions-- (and of course the logger-specific level overrides enabled by `MinimumLevel.Override()`).

In Serilog configuration, if level overrides and the `Fatal` level are insufficient to suppress these messages, it's always possible to specify `SourceContext <> 'Microsoft.AspNetCore.Diagnostics.ExceptionHandlerMiddleware'` as a filter.
Filtering them out is what I ended up doing.

review_comments: @davidfowl are we really doing this? I can't think of anywhere else in the framework that you can control logging on a component via its options. Is this case special because if you handle the error then it should no longer be logged at the error level? If this exception is considered handled then maybe we should instead downgrade it to info or debug.
@jez9999 would downgrading the log level used here help in your scenario?
Yea I thought we resolved the issue tbh. Not sure why were fixing this when it's possible to suppress the log. I guess this is more discoverable but as you say, we don't do this anywhere else
Dunno, I think the "None" logging option was ok, it's just a shame Serilog doesn't support it.  Not ASP.NET Core's fault though.  However Serilog filters can be used instead.
Ok, closing this PR and issue as resolved then.
I don't think we need several new overloads, this is very niche. The new property on ExceptionHandlerOptions should be adequate.
